summary: Conducted independent keyword-cannibalization audit of 89 content pages based on front matter extraction. Produced a definitive adjudication map for 9 suspect sets, identified the top-5 search-visibility blockers, and flagged 3 high-risk duplicative assets threatening net-negative indexing status.
findings: [OBSERVED] BLOCKER #1: State Data Collision. '2026-utility-cost-index-by-state.md' and 'average-utility-bills-by-state-2026.md' target identical queries ('average utility bill by state 2026') and contain conflicting aliases proving prior, incomplete consolidation attempts. [INFERENCE] Link equity and SERP dominance are fractured for a high-value commercial-intent cluster. Winner: '2026-utility-cost-index-by-state'. Disposition: 301 redirect loser to winner.

[OBSERVED] BLOCKER #2: 'Read Your Bill' Fragmentation. Four distinct pages ('01-how-to-read-your-electric-bill', 'how-to-read-your-utility-bill', 'complete-guide-understanding-utility-bill', 'electric-bill-breakdown-understanding-line-items') compete for near-identical root queries. 'complete-guide...' explicitly aliases to 'how-to-read-your-utility-bill'. [INFERENCE] Internal competition blunts topical authority for the site's highest-volume utility-literacy keywords. Winners: '01...' (Electric) and 'how-to-read-your-utility-bill' (Generic). Losers: 'electric-bill-breakdown...' and 'complete-guide...' should be redirected/merged.

[OBSERVED] BLOCKER #3: Delivery/Supply Redundancy. '24-delivery-charge-vs-supply-charge-utility-bill.md', 'supply-vs-delivery-charges-electricity.md', and 'gas-delivery-charge-vs-supply-charge.md' all cover delivery vs. supply charges. '24...' holds an alias to the electricity-specific slug, indicating a past merge. [INFERENCE] Without explicit canonical enforcement, three URLs fragment crawl budget and relevance scores for a foundational utility concept. Winner: '24...' (broadest reach). Disposition: 'supply-vs-delivery-charges-electricity' requires immediate 301 to '24...'; 'gas-delivery...' remains valid but needs differentiated H1/keyword targeting from '24...'.

[OBSERVED] BLOCKER #4: Customer Charge Duplication. '17-what-is-customer-charge-on-utility-bill.md' possesses an alias pointing to '/blog/gas-customer-charge-explained/', yet the dedicated 'gas-customer-charge-explained.md' file remains active. [INFERENCE] Exact-match keyword overlap on 'customer charge' creates duplicate indexing risk. Disposition: Redirect 'gas-customer-charge-explained.md' into '17...'.

[OBSERVED] BLOCKER #5: High-Bill Intent Sprawl. 23+ pages broadly target 'high bill', spanning electric ('03-why-is-my-electric-bill-so-high.md'), water ('06-water-bill-too-high.md', 'why-did-my-water-bill-suddenly-increase.md', seasonal variants), and gas ('07-gas-bill-too-high.md'). [INFERENCE] Broad 'high bill' searches lack a single authoritative diagnostic pillar, causing internal resource division and allowing competitors to aggregate intent across verticals more efficiently.

[INFERENCE] Meter Reading & KWh Clusters: '11-understanding-kwh-usage.md' (Bill analysis intent) vs 'what-is-a-kilowatt-hour.md' (Definition intent) are semantically distinct and safe. Similarly, meter-reading pages (dial, digital, smart, water, gas) serve distinct long-tail queries with minimal overlap. No intervention required.

[OBSERVED] NET-NEGATIVE ASSETS: Pages that attract crawl budget, dilute domain authority, and fail to satisfy a unique user intent. 1) 'average-utility-bills-by-state-2026.md': If it renders to a standalone URL without a canonical pointing to '2026-utility-cost-index-by-state.md', it is pure duplicative weight. 2) 'electric-bill-breakdown-understanding-line-items.md': Highly likely to rank below '01-how-to-read-your-electric-bill.md' for its own targeted terms, serving no standalone value and bleeding anchor text. 3) 'complete-guide-understanding-utility-bill.md': Explicitly aliased to another page in FM; if it still generates a standalone page in 'public/', it is pure cannibalization noise. Disposition: Immediate 301 redirects for all three.

        print(f"\n[MISSING] {name} - No files found!")

    for m in matches:
        print(f"  [{m['path']}] T: {m['title']} | K: {m['keywords']} | A: {m['alias']}")

]

    "Delivery & Supply": ["24-delivery", "supply-vs-delivery", "gas-delivery", "how-utility-rates"],
    "Customer Charge": ["customer-charge"],
    "Water Bill High": ["water-bill-too-high", "why-did-my-water-bill-suddenly-increase", "how-to-lower-water-bill"],
